example_text: As for the family.
Sori usually at the fork of a vein, or seated on a simple vein
near base with many thick conical spines to 2 mm long
veins to 12 pairs
scales flabelloid, near base, dark, shining, to 20 x 1.5 mm, with fragile edges mostly abraded
Scales and hairs: costa glabrescent and warty near base
costulets 5--6 mm apart
Trunk nearly always erect, short or tall, rarely absent, (rarely prostrate, not in our area)
indusium a firm brown scale of rather irregular shape on costular side, often nearly circular, sometimes unevenly lobed, rarely extending round base of receptacle on side remote from costule
larger ones c. 2.5 cm apart
pinnules sessile, rather easily detached when dry
paraphyses usually present as multicellular hairs, sometimes flat and several cells wide at base
median to lowest pinnae free, with pinnules deeply lobed to costulets, pinnules to c. 6.5 x 1.2 cm, segments slightly falcate, costulets 12--18 mm apart, all pinnae with sori on fertile lamina
also firm brown elongate scales, rather slender, the larger ones with a dark setiform apex and sometimes dark marginal setae
lamina-segments rather thin
pinnae normally pinnate-bipinnatifid, in a few cases simple, fully bipinnate or tripinnate, sometimes dimorphic
rachises medium to dark brown, almost glabrous below, appressed hairy above
paraphyses numerous, translucent to dark brown, hardly exceeding the sporangia
lobes separated by intervals of about their own width
pinnules almost symmetrical at the base, many on each pinna subequal, distal ones more-or-less abruptly decreasing

Pneumathodes present in a discontinuous line (or 2--3 lines close together) along each side of stipe and rachis, in subgenus Cyathea converging downwards on each side of base of stipe and there oft...
receptacles swollen
bullate scales on costulets, often deciduously from fertile pinnules
the larger ones lobed halfway to costulet, veins in such lobes pinnate
edges more-or-less crenate-serrate
upper surface of costa and costule raised
thinly papyraceous, veins forked, distinct on both surfaces
lobes oblique
Stipes dark brown
costa brown or paler, purplish at basal portion

indusium attached all round base of receptacle and covering young sorus, opening to form a firm-edged cup or opening by irregular rupture, or attached on costulet side of receptacle and of varying ...
the apical pinna usually like the others, and all pinnae articulate to the rachis
lobed almost to costules
rachis and costa glabrescent on lower surface
Scales and hairs: scales on costules and costulets beneath sparse
in some species of subgenus Sphaeropteris scales present round base of receptacle more-or-less covering young sporangia
Spores thin-walled, smooth or papillose
sometimes with lateral buds forming small crowns of fronds, old fronds persistent and hanging down over the trunk
veins simple or branched, lower ones usually once forked, sometimes pinnate where pinnule-segments are deeply lobed
Gametophytes green, cordate
indusium firm, shining brown when old, at first ovoid with a small apical aperture, breaking irregularly and persistent
Laminae rigid, pinnae drying very dark
Fronds more-or-less elliptical, lower pinnae always smaller than middle ones, sometimes gradually much reduced and then the stipe short
paraphyses shorter than sporangia, some near apex of receptacle broad and scale-like at base
entire or the largest crenate or toothed towards the apex, slightly oblique, slightly or hardly falcate
receptacle erect, club-shaped to spherical
without bullate scales
Sori a few to numerous, close to costulet, indusium a small dark scale on costular side
Sporangia many, always short-stalked
Stems with polycyclic dictyosteles, apices (and usually petiole bases) covered with large scales, sometimes also with scurf (small scales) or hairs
Scales present on lower and lateral surfaces of axes of frond, at least in early stages of growth, larger ones on stipe and on lower surfaces of axes and veins, rarely on lamina between veins
veins glabrous except for occasional hairs on upper surface
